glossary.bedbound: Unable to get out of bed.
glossary.immobility: Being unable to move or change position easily.
glossary.spinal cord injury: Damage to the spinal cord causing loss of movement and sensation below the level.
glossary.malnutrition: Poor nutritional state from inadequate intake of energy, protein or nutrients.
glossary.incontinence: Involuntary leakage of urine or faeces.
glossary.elbows: A common pressure point in bedbound patients.
glossary.heels: A common pressure point because bone lies just under the skin.
glossary.sacral: Relating to the sacrum at the base of the spine.
glossary.skin ulcer: A break in the skin that fails to heal.
glossary.lab marker: A blood test result that indicates a disease.
glossary.muscle, tendon or bone: Deep structures exposed in a stage 4 ulcer.
glossary.tendon: Tough cord joining muscle to bone.
glossary.infection: Invasion and multiplication of microbes in body tissue.
glossary.sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated response to infection.
glossary.non-healing: Failing to heal despite treatment, usually over weeks.
glossary.systemic illness: Being unwell throughout the body, for example fever and tachycardia.
glossary.sterile saline: Germ-free salt water used to clean wounds.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging, a detailed scan used to look for bone or deep soft tissue infection.
glossary.lumbar spine: The lower back part of the spine.
glossary.pressure-relieving devices: Special mattresses and cushions that spread weight to reduce pressure on bony points.
glossary.moist wound dressings: Dressings that keep the wound moist, which speeds healing.
glossary.penicillin allergic: Allergy to penicillin antibiotics such as flucloxacillin and amoxicillin.
glossary.microvasculature: The smallest blood vessels: arterioles, capillaries and venules.
glossary.collagen synthesis: Making collagen, the main structural protein of skin and scars.
glossary.wound healing: The process of repairing damaged tissue.
glossary.susceptibility: How likely someone is to be affected.
glossary.epidermal: Relating to the epidermis, the outer layer of skin.
glossary.capillaries: The tiniest blood vessels, where oxygen passes to the tissues.
glossary.reconstruction: Surgery to rebuild tissue, often with skin or muscle flaps.
